name: Jharokha
line: Carved haveli doors open at dusk onto a courtyard of diyas and marigolds, in sindoor, marigold and gold.

name: Ivory
line: A blind-embossed ivory envelope, sealed in wax, inspired by Lucknow's white-on-white chikankari.

name: Deepotsav
line: Diya by diya, the ghats of Ayodhya light up, the Ram Mandir glows, and your names appear in the night sky. With a Ram Darbar blessing.

name: Jharokha Film
line: Jharokha as a film: the carved haveli doors swing open and your guests walk into a courtyard lit with diyas.

name: Ivory Film
line: Ivory as a film: the wax seal cracks and the embossed flaps open one by one in soft window light.

name: Zardozi
line: A maroon velvet envelope worked in gold zardozi, sealed with your initials. It opens flap by flap onto your invitation card.

name: Moti
line: A jewellery box inlaid with mother-of-pearl, a string of pearls round its clasp. The pearls slip away, the lid lifts, and your card is waiting inside.

name: Noor
line: An emerald silk folio with carved ivory jaali doors, made for your nikah. Tap it, a little lantern glows warm, and your card is waiting inside.

name: Mehtab
line: Made for your nikah and walima. Carved palace doors swing open on a moonlit courtyard, and your names are written among the stars.

name: Roshni
line: Red silk and ivory jaali doors, made for your pheras. A lantern glows, the doors open, and your wedding is under a red mandap of jasmine.

name: Kamal
line: A lotus pond at first light. A boat of flowers drifts to the middle, and your names appear on the still water.

name: Rangeelo
line: A painted pink city where kites fill the sky. One tap and a block-printed cloth unrolls down the haveli wall with your names.

name: Mithai
line: Good news comes with mithai. A rani pink box with a gold lid opens on kaju katli, laddoos and your invitation card.

name: Kanjivaram
line: Your invitation arrives wrapped in rani pink Kanjivaram silk and tied with jasmine. The silk opens like a saree’s fold onto your card.

name: Phulkari
line: Your invitation arrives folded in a golden phulkari, tied with a parandi. A hand unties the parandi and the cloth opens onto your card.

name: Sheesh Mahal
line: A mirror palace in the dark. One lamp is lit, a thousand mirrors catch it, and your names wait in the glowing arch.

name: Photobooth
line: A brass frame on red velvet. One tap, a flash, and a strip of your own photos prints out, then the date.

name: Pichwai
line: A lotus pond in the Nathdwara painting style that opens at dawn under the guest's thumb.

name: Temple
line: A gopuram at dusk, a brass kuthuvilakku the guest lights, and a gold border on ivory.

name: Mehfil
line: A palace hall at night, lit one candle at a time, for sangeet nights and night weddings.

name: Akhbaar
line: Your big news makes the front page. Your names in the headline, your photo in print, the date in the dateline.

name: Genda
line: Strings of marigolds part at your guest's touch and open onto a sunlit haldi courtyard, all turmeric yellow and mehndi green.

name: Hum Dono
line: Meet the couple: your photo on a scrapbook page, an arrow for each of you, and stickers of everything you love.

name: Parda
line: Red velvet curtains part under a crystal chandelier, and your names are waiting on the stage.

name: Safar
line: Your two hometowns joined by a route, a little plane flying everyone in, and a boarding pass for every family's reply.

name: Shubho Drishti
line: Two paan leaves part for the first look, and there are your names. Made for Bengali weddings, in alta red, shola white and gold.
